findings.explanation: The message uses urgency, a threat, or a deadline. Pressure to act quickly is a common tactic to stop people from checking whether a request is genuine.
The message asks for an OTP, PIN, password, or banking details. These are meant to be kept secret; sharing them can give someone else access to your account.

The message contains a link. Do not open it unless you have confirmed the sender through an official channel. This link uses a link-shortening service, which hides the real destination; uses unencrypted http.

Record of a suspicious message
Prepared with Second Look on 2026-10-12.
This is a record of a message I received. It is not a finding that the message is fraudulent.

The message, exactly as I received it:
URGENT: Your SBI account will be blocked today. Update your KYC at http://bit.ly/kyc-update and share the OTP you receive.

What I have done so far: I paid, or money has left my account

Warning signs noticed by Second Look's rule-based checks:
- Urgency, a threat or a deadline: "URGENT"
- Asks for an OTP, PIN, password or banking details: "update and share the OTP"
- Contains a link: "http://bit.ly/kyc-update"

Where to report:
The I4C website tells people to report cybercrime by calling the helpline 1930. (Source: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, https://i4c.mha.gov.in/)
